question: I bought as a company and need our address and VAT ID on the invoices, but I already paid. Can I add it now?
reference_answer: Yes, open any invoice from Paddle and click Add address & VAT Number. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on, but invoices already issued stay as they were. With a valid VAT ID no VAT is charged on future payments, except for UK businesses, which still pay UK VAT they can reclaim.
key_facts: Open an invoice and click Add address & VAT Number
Details appear on invoices from then on; already-issued invoices stay as they were
No VAT on future payments with a valid VAT ID
UK businesses still pay UK VAT

evidence.title: View and save your invoices
evidence.text:
Our payment processor Paddle sends an invoice by email automatically after each payment. You can also view past invoices from your Plausible account. Paddle doesn't issue credit notes or receipts for refunds, so a refund has no separate document.

Log in to your Plausible account. In the top right menu, click your account name and open the settings. Scroll down in the **Subscription** section to see a list of all invoices. Select an invoice to open it in a new browser tab.

To save a PDF copy, use your browser's **Print** command and select **Save as PDF** as the destination.

Invoice list in Plausible settings

## Add your company address and VAT number

Open any invoice from Paddle and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Paddle handles VAT and sales taxes. If you provide a valid VAT ID, no VAT will be charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. When Paddle refunds the VAT on a payment after accepting your VAT number, it doesn't send a separate credit note. Instead, it reissues that payment's invoice without VAT, and the reissued invoice is the one for your records. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

## Change your billing address

Open any invoice and click **Edit business address** to update your address.

Changing the **country** on an existing subscription isn't possible due to tax regulations. To switch countries, cancel your subscription a day or two before your next renewal, then subscribe again right away from the same account with the new country (see How do I change the country on my subscription?). No data is lost in this process.

evidence.title: Billing FAQ
evidence.text:
If you're purchasing on behalf of a business, click **Add VAT number** on the second step of the checkout, where you also add your payment details. Paddle handles all sales tax calculations and will apply the correct rate based on your details.

Add VAT number at checkout

If you missed this step, open your most recent Paddle invoice and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Once Paddle accepts a valid VAT number, no VAT is charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

Paddle checks EU VAT numbers against the EU's VIES database. If your number shows as invalid, check it there first: a number that isn't registered in VIES for trade between EU countries can't be accepted, even when it's valid in your own country.

Note: Block both IPv4 and IPv6 if your device uses both
Most modern devices and networks have both an IPv4 address (e.g. `203.0.113.5`) and an IPv6 address (e.g. `2001:db8::1`). Your browser or network proxy may send visits using either one depending on the connection.

If you block only your IPv4 address but your browser sends a request over IPv6, that visit will still be recorded. To reliably exclude your traffic, check whether your device has both address types and add each one separately.

The **block your current IP** button captures whichever address your browser is currently using. Click it, then visit a site like whatismyipaddress.com to check whether you also have a second address type, and add that manually if so.

question: My thank-you page keeps recording extra purchases when customers reload it. How do I stop the revenue being counted twice?
reference_answer: Reloaded thank-you pages fire the purchase event again and add more conversions and revenue. You can remove the trigger from the URL after sending using `history.replaceState`, send from a checkout callback instead of a page, ignore old checkouts on your server, or mark the order as tracked in your own store.
key_facts: Reloading a thank-you page can fire the purchase event again
Remove the trigger from the URL with history.replaceState after sending
Alternatively send from a callback, ignore old checkouts on the server or mark orders as tracked
answer:
To stop purchases from being counted twice when thank-you pages are reloaded, bookmarked, or reopened, you can use one of these approaches:
- If your page sends the event only when the URL carries a checkout ID or amount, call `history.replaceState(null, '', location.pathname)` right after `plausible(...)` [1]. A reload then has nothing to send [1]. No storage needed [1].
- Send from a callback, not a page [1]. Overlay checkouts (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) fire their success callback once per payment [1].
- Ignore old checkouts on the server [1]. When you look up the payment on your server, skip the event if the payment was created long ago (for example, Stripe's Checkout Session `created` timestamp is more than an hour old) [1].
- Mark the order in your own store [1]. If you already keep orders in a database, you can mark an order as tracked the first time the thank-you page renders, like our WordPress plugin does for WooCommerce orders [1]. Nothing extra is sent to Plausible [1].

citations.quote: - **Remove the trigger from the URL after sending.** If your page sends the event only when the URL carries a checkout ID or amount, call `history.replaceState(null, '', location.pathname)` right after `plausible(...)`. A reload then has nothing to send. No storage needed.
- **Send from a callback, not a page.** Overlay checkouts (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) fire their success callback once per payment.

- **Ignore old checkouts on the server.** When you look up the payment on your server, skip the event if the payment was created long ago (for example, Stripe's Checkout Session `created` timestamp is more than an hour old).

- **Mark the order in your own store.** If you already keep orders in a database, you can mark an order as tracked the first time the thank-you page renders, like our WordPress plugin does for WooCommerce orders. Nothing extra is sent to Plausible.

evidence.title: Ecommerce revenue and attribution tracking
evidence.text:
**One purchase event vs. per-product events**

The simplest approach is a single `Purchase` event with the total order value. This gives you clean revenue totals, referral attribution and conversion rates without complex setup.

If you need to break down revenue by product type, category or subscription tier, use custom properties alongside the revenue event. For example:

```js
plausible('Purchase', {revenue: {currency: 'USD', amount: 49.00}, props: {plan: 'Pro'}})
```

This lets you filter the revenue report by `plan` to compare revenue from different product lines.

**Where to fire the event**

Fire the revenue event on your order confirmation or thank you page, not on the checkout button click. Firing on button click captures intent but not completed purchases, which inflates revenue figures and makes attribution misleading.

For subscription upgrades, fire on the confirmation page after payment is processed, not when the user selects a plan.

**Count each purchase only once**

Thank-you pages get reloaded, bookmarked and reopened. Every time the purchase event fires again, it adds another conversion and more revenue. Use one of these:

Thank-you pages get reloaded, bookmarked and reopened. Every time the purchase event fires again, it adds another conversion and more revenue. Use one of these:

- **Remove the trigger from the URL after sending.** If your page sends the event only when the URL carries a checkout ID or amount, call `history.replaceState(null, '', location.pathname)` right after `plausible(...)`. A reload then has nothing to send. No storage needed.
- **Send from a callback, not a page.** Overlay checkouts (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) fire their success callback once per payment.
- **Ignore old checkouts on the server.** When you look up the payment on your server, skip the event if the payment was created long ago (for example, Stripe's Checkout Session `created` timestamp is more than an hour old).
- **Mark the order in your own store.** If you already keep orders in a database, you can mark an order as tracked the first time the thank-you page renders, like our WordPress plugin does for WooCommerce orders. Nothing extra is sent to Plausible.

question: Why do I see (none) all over my custom properties report even though I didn't filter by anything?
reference_answer: When you view the Properties tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard, including regular pageviews, and many of those don't have the property attached. That's why you see `(none)`. It also appears when a property is sent with no value, as null or undefined, or with some events but not others.

Without a custom event filter the tab includes all pageviews
Null or undefined values also show as (none)
answer: When you are viewing the Properties tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard including regular pageviews, and many of these events may not have a property attached [1]. `(none)` can also appear because you sent a `null` or `undefined` value, or sent the property with some events but not all [2].

citations.quote: However, if you're viewing the **Properties** tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard (including all regular pageviews) and many of these events may not have a property attached. This is why you see the `(none)` value.

`(none)` can appear for several reasons, including sending a `null` or `undefined` value, sending the property with some events but not all, or viewing the Properties tab without a custom event filter applied.

evidence.title: Custom properties
evidence.text:
Plausible will display `(none)` in your dashboard when you send a custom property key with no value, or `null`/`undefined` as a value. Also, when you send one event with a property (e.g. `author`) and another event with the same name, but without the `author` property, then you will also see the `(none)` value because the property has not been sent with every event.

When you filter your dashboard by a particular custom event and look at the **Properties** tab, you should only see `(none)` if some of those events were sent without the property. However, if you're viewing the **Properties** tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard (including all regular pageviews) and many of these events may not have a property attached. This is why you see the `(none)` value.

evidence.title: Custom event tracking
evidence.text: `(none)` can appear for several reasons, including sending a `null` or `undefined` value, sending the property with some events but not all, or viewing the Properties tab without a custom event filter applied. See Custom Properties: (none) values for the full explanation. For troubleshooting: confirm the property value is not `null` or `undefined` at the moment the event fires, and that the property name is spelled exactly the same way in every event call.

question: My site search shows results without changing the URL, so I can't see what people search for. How can I track it?
reference_answer: Send a custom event from your search code whenever a search is made, for example `plausible("Site Search", { props: { search_term: term } })`, and add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings. Custom events count towards your billable pageviews.
key_facts: Send a Site Search custom event with a search_term prop from your search code
Add Site Search as a custom event goal
Custom events count towards billable pageviews
answer:
Some search boxes show results without loading a new page, so the term never appears in the address [1]. In that case, send a custom event from your search code when a search is made [1]:

```javascript
plausible("Site Search", { props: { search_term: term } })
```

Replace `term` with the variable that holds what the visitor typed [1]. Then add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings [1].
